title: The Serpins Are an Expanding Superfamily of Structurally Similar but Functionally Diverse Proteins
abstract: The serpins (serine proteinase inhibitors) are a superfamily of proteins (350–500 amino acids in size) that fold into a conserved structure and employ a unique suicide substrate-like inhibitory mechanism. The serpins were last reviewed in 1994 (1).
